clue.text: Following delay of months, slander hospital department's union

indicators.note: a delayed letter turns up later, so it is moved from the front to the back of the word

parts.note: to malign someone is to slander them
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: After months of waiting, a hospital unit's alliance is slandered.
explanation.walkthrough: MALIGN with its M pushed to the end becomes ALIGNM.
explanation.definitionFit: An alignment is an alliance or a coming together of parties, so it can mean union.

clue.text: Fools judge? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the word: its last letter goes

parts.note: a six-letter verb for judge or evaluate, stopped one letter short

explanation.surface: A sneer at the bench: judges are fools, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun, a person on the bench, which fits the insult; it is the verb, to assess, docked its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the donkey's name has long been the everyday word for a stupid person.

clue.text: People from Indiana share twin sons

parts.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for Indiana
a divi is a dividend, a share of profits
twin = dual, as in twin/dual controls
s = son(s), from genealogies

explanation.surface: Hoosiers split the family estate between twin boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People from Indiana' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'People', and 'from' belongs to it as the link. Divi is a British shortening of dividend.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: persons counted singly, as in 'three people' or 'three separate persons'.

clue.text: Head of state no longer in charge following union of cardinals

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective: relating to numbers, which cardinals are

indicators.note: following means the queen and the in-charge letters come after the union
no longer marks the head of state as a former one, the late Queen; it adds no letters of its own

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the late Queen, a former head of state

explanation.surface: A former head of state returns to power after cardinals unite, as at a papal conclave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' is not a deletion: it qualifies the head of state as the late Queen, ER. Cardinals look like churchmen, but here they are cardinal numbers: one, two, three.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers express quantity, so something of cardinals is made of figures.

clue.text: Defective electronic chip's core codes formed imitative words

parts.note: e- = electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: a faulty set of letters is to be rebuilt
the middle letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the middle two letters of CHIP
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faulty chip scrambles its codes into gibberish noises.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole verb phrase: to echoise is to make words that imitate sounds, like 'buzz'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense: to echoise is to coin onomatopoeic words, those that mimic the sound they name.

clue.text: Breaking in, tense street urchin lowering head

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first letter is lowered to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a gamin is a street urchin

explanation.surface: A nervous street kid ducks his head while breaking into a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking in' looks like burglary, but it means training a horse. GAMIN's G drops to the end, giving AMING.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking in a horse means training it to accept a rider, which is taming it.

clue.text: Public school lodge reported

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, not read

parts.note: to lodge something is to stow it

explanation.surface: A news item about a public school's lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is a well-known English boarding school; in Britain 'public school' means a private fee-paying one.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the famous fee-paying boarding schools, in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Hurt forces brought up case for three days

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to ram is to force, so forces is rams

indicators.note: case for takes the outside letters of three

explanation.surface: Troops were wounded and sent home in a case lasting three days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks like a noun for troops, but it is a verb here: to ram is to force. D for days is the dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarted means stung or felt a sharp pain, so it means ached or felt sore.

clue.text: Old newspaper much of the time in verse?

definitions.text: much of the time in verse

parts.note: o = old
FT = the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A defunct paper that ran poetry most days.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a British daily. 'Oft' is the poets' word for often.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is a poetic word for often, much of the time.

clue.text: Continental jargon primarily used in sensitive, regressive summit

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the reversed word
regressive means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a sore spot is sensitive

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: European officialese is used mainly at a touchy summit that goes backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily used' looks like it could mean 'chiefly employed', but it just picks the first letter, which goes into the touchy word once that word has been turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Europeak is jargon associated with European Union officials, so it is the jargon of the Continent.

clue.text: Depraved scene from "love party" embodied by aggressive-submissive proclivity

parts.note: S&M, sadomasochism
love = nil = O, in tennis
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A racy orgy description, the kind of scene a tabloid would relish.
explanation.walkthrough: S&M is sadomasochism, the 'aggressive-submissive proclivity', reduced to its two initials, which then wrap around the love and the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom, the Biblical city, is the byword for a depraved place.

clue.text: Second-rate artiste carrying more weight on thigh

parts.note: the ham is the back of the thigh
fatter = heavier

explanation.surface: A mediocre performer putting weight on around the thighs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-rate artiste' suggests HAM, which the answer does contain, but the ham in the wordplay is the thigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamfatter is an old term for an incompetent, ranting actor.

clue.text: Monarchies asserting vetoes abroad

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: Kingdoms flexing their veto rights in foreign affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: independent countries need not have kings, but a monarchy is literally a nation ruled by a sovereign, which is the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on sovereign: a king or queen is a sovereign, so a kingdom is read as a nation belonging to one.

clue.text: Film of Charles upset Diana briefly

parts.note: Charles III is the king

indicators.note: upset means the shortened name is knocked over into a new order
briefly means the name is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Charles upset Diana for a short while, as a royal tabloid story might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts DIANA to DIAN, which 'upset' rearranges into ANDI.
explanation.definitionFit: The King and I is a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical made into a 1956 movie.

clue.text: Took away cover from discharge pipe examined at both ends

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside letters
keep only the first and last letters

parts.note: D and E, the outside of DISCHARGE
a duct is a pipe
E and D, the ends of EXAMINED

explanation.surface: A plumber removes the cover of a waste pipe and inspects both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took away cover' reads as one action; the definition stops at 'Took away', as in subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Deducted means took away, as a sum from a total.

clue.text: Dry ditty regularly confused with 14

indicators.note: confused with means these letters are mixed together with the other answer into a new order
regularly takes every other letter of ditty, starting with the first

parts.note: 14 refers to the answer to clue 14, ADHERE

explanation.surface: A dry song gets muddled up with another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' gives DTY from ditty; mix those with ADHERE, the answer to 14.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate is to remove water from something, so to desiccate it.

clue.text: Stick notice in The Times?

parts.note: an ad is a notice
the clue is printed in The Times, so 'in The Times' is here

explanation.surface: Posting a notice in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the self-reference: this very puzzle is in The Times, so its location is HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: glue makes things stick, cling fast to a surface.

clue.text: Scold Henry in school, location of Maggie's education

indicators.note: 'in school' puts the scolding and Henry inside the school, as a pupil sits in one

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
to rant is to scold loudly
H = henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A teacher tells off a pupil called Henry at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Maggie is Margaret Thatcher, who grew up and went to school in Grantham, a Lincolnshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Grantham is where Margaret Thatcher was born and educated.

clue.text: Catch securing edges of door-plate in tank

definitions.note: header tank: the answer is the word that goes with tank

indicators.note: securing means the word for catch holds the edge letters fast inside

parts.note: to catch a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: edges of takes the first and last letters of door-plate

explanation.surface: A latch fixing the edges of a plate on the door of a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links: a header tank is a raised water tank feeding a central heating system.
explanation.definitionFit: A header tank is a raised cistern feeding water by gravity into a system.

clue.text: Met maker of saw that's turned up in River Dee

indicators.note: in means the reversed saw word sits inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that's turned up is read upwards

parts.note: to rip is to saw wood along the grain, as with a ripsaw
dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: Someone met the man who made a saw, found turned up in the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Dee' looks like one river; it is two pieces, a river (the Exe, in south-west England) and the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet one's maker is to die, and expired means died.

clue.text: Good buzz surrounding Polish play in Rugby

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so 'good buzz' is wrapped around the polish

parts.note: g = good
a kick is a thrill, a buzz
to polish is to rub

explanation.surface: A Polish player gives a good buzz to a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Polish is disguise: it is the verb polish. A grub kick is a low kick along the ground in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a low punt that skids along the ground, one kicking option in rugby.

clue.text: Incorporate legal draft delivered prior to crash

indicators.note: prior to means the sounded word comes before the word for crash
delivered means spoken, so the word for legal draft is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a bill is a draft of a new law
a din is a loud crashing noise

explanation.surface: A draft law is passed just before a market crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To build in is to make a feature an integral part of something from the start.

clue.text: Fat cat completely extra

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a wealthy person
all = completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A plutocrat who is completely surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a no-ball is an illegal delivery, and the run it gives away counts as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-ball is one kind of extra in cricket scoring.

clue.text: Regrettably, couple that initiates divorce furtive about settling

indicators.note: couple that initiates takes the first two letters of divorce
about means the furtive word goes around the settling word

parts.note: sly means furtive
appointing a date is settling it

explanation.surface: Sadly, one half of a sly couple starts a divorce while settling.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointingly means in a way that lets one down, so it is said with regret.

clue.text: Second person finally seen collecting litter?

parts.note: 'you' is the second-person pronoun

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the last letters of SEEN and COLLECTING

explanation.surface: Another person is spotted picking up rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The litter is not rubbish but a litter of pups or kittens; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is an animal's young, born together.

clue.text: Bizarre dream, not the first that involves intro to Finnegans Wake

indicators.note: bizarre means weird, so these letters are twisted into a new order
not the first means dream loses its opening letter
intro to takes the first letter of Finnegans

explanation.surface: A weird dream connected with James Joyce's novel Finnegans Wake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finnegans Wake' looks like a title, but the final word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The wake of a ship is the trail behind it, so figuratively the consequences that follow an event.

clue.text: Leading trio to sign letter overseas

indicators.note: take the first three letters

parts.note: the first three letters of TAURUS, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Three leaders sign a letter abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The sign must be found before its first three letters can be taken; 'overseas' marks the letter as foreign, here Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Greek equivalent of T, a letter used abroad.

clue.text: London authority protects river for locals

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: lonDON AUthority

explanation.surface: London's governing body shields a river for its residents.
explanation.walkthrough: The locals are German and Austrian speakers: Donau is their name for the Danube, not a London river.
explanation.definitionFit: Donau is the German name for the Danube, the river as locals call it.

clue.text: Horse bet, essentially £1

indicators.note: the essence of BET is its middle letter

parts.note: middle letter of BET
a quid is British slang for a pound

explanation.surface: A one-pound flutter on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse bet' reads as a single phrase, but the definition is only 'Horse'; the bet gives its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An equid is any member of the horse family.

clue.text: Soldiers charging Roman Catholic gathering ultimately feeling sorrow

parts.note: the Latin rite is the Roman Catholic Church's
men = soldiers, other ranks

indicators.note: take the last letter of GATHERING

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: Troops storm a Catholic assembly, and grief follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman Catholic gathering' looks like one phrase, a Mass; 'gathering' only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to mourn aloud, grieving over a loss.
